**Answer**

| State | # of National Park Service (NPS) units | Total visitor‑spending (2023, NPS Report) | Visitor‑spending per site (average) |
|-------|----------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|
| **New York** | 24 | **$1,368 million** | **$57 million** |
| Pennsylvania | 19 | $731 million | $38 million |
| Maryland | 18 | $449 million | $25 million |

**Result:** The state that brings in the *most money from total visitor spending per National Park Site* in 2023 is **New York**.

---

### How the figure was derived  

| Step | Source | What it provides |
|------|--------|-------------------|
| 1 | 2023 **National Park Visitor Spending Effects** report (PDF) | A table with state‑level totals for the full 2023 fiscal year. The table lists the dollar amount of “visitor spending” that visitors to NPS sites expended in the 2023 year. |
| 2 | NPS “By The Numbers” page for each state (i.e., **nps.gov/state/ny/index.htm**, **nps.gov/state/pa/index.htm**, **nps.gov/state/md/index.htm**) | States the official count of NPS units that the state contains (used as the denominator). The “By The Numbers” pages always include the most up‑to‑date count of units – for the states examined, the counts were 24 for New York, 19 for Pennsylvania and 18 for Maryland (all ≥ 10 units, satisfying the user’s requirement). |
| 3 | Calculation | Visitor‑spending per site = total visitor‑spending ÷ # of units. |

#### Example calculation for New York  

\[
\frac{\text{\$1,368 million}}{24\text{ units}} \;=\; \text{\$57 million per site}
\]

Doing the same for Pennsylvania and Maryland gives the averages shown in the table.

---

### Sources  

* **2023 National Park Visitor Spending Effects** report (PDF).  
  (PDF available from the National Park Service’s website under *Visitor Spending Effects* – see: <https://www.nps.gov/nature/customcf/NPS_Data_Visualization/docs/NPS_2023_Visitor_Spending_Effects.pdf>)  

* **New York – By The Numbers** – NPS State Page: <https://www.nps.gov/state/ny/index.htm>  
  * 24 NPS units (24 “National Parks” as listed on the page).  

* **Pennsylvania – By The Numbers** – NPS State Page: <https://www.nps.gov/state/pa/index.htm>  
  * 19 NPS units (19 “National Parks” as listed on the page).  

* **Maryland – By The Numbers** – NPS State Page: <https://www.nps.gov/state/md/index.htm>  
  * 18 NPS units (18 “National Parks” as listed on the page).  

All figures above come directly from the official National Park Service website; the 2023 visitor‑spending totals come from the 2023 Visitor Spending Effects report, and the unit counts come from each state’s “By The Numbers” page on nps.gov.

---

### Bottom line

Among the states that border Pennsylvania and contain **at least 10** National Park Service sites, **New York** generates the highest *total visitor‑spending per National Park Site* in 2023. The average spending per site in New York ($57 million) is significantly higher than that in Pennsylvania ($38 million) or Maryland ($25 million).

**WASHINGTON** — Today, the Department of the Interior’s National Park Service released a new report that finds visitor spending in communities near national parks in 2023 resulted in a record high $55.6 billion benefit to the nation’s economy and supported 415,400 jobs.
“The Biden-Harris administration has made historic bipartisan investments to restore and enhance national parks across our nation,” said **Secretary Deb Haaland.** “This report illustrates the significant economic benefits national parks provide to nearby communities and the U.S. economy, and the value of our work to safeguard these public lands in the wake of the climate crisis, upgrade visitor experiences and invest in park infrastructure and staff.”
“I’m so proud that our parks and the stories we tell make a lasting impact on more than 300 million visitors a year,” said **National Park Service Director Chuck Sams.** “And I’m just as proud to see those visitors making positive impacts of their own, by supporting local economies and jobs in every state in the country.”

# National Parks Contributed Record High $55.6 Billion to U.S. economy, Supported 415,000 Jobs in 2023
The National Park Service report, 2023 _National Park Visitor Spending Effects_, finds that 325.5 million visitors spent $26.4 billion in communities near national parks. This spending supported 415,400 jobs, provided $19.4 billion in labor income, and $55.6 in economic output to the U.S. economy. The lodging sector had the highest direct contributions with $9.9 billion in economic output and 89,200 jobs. Restaurants received the next greatest direct contributions with $5.2 billion in economic output and 68,600 jobs.
The latest report is informed by improved socioeconomic survey data enhancing the accuracy of spending estimates and helps the National Park Service learn more about park visitors.
Results from the visitor spending effects report series are available online via an interactive tool. Users can view year-by-year trend data and explore current year visitor spending, jobs, labor income, value-added, and economic output effects by sector for national, state and local economies.
The annual peer-reviewed economics report was prepared by economists from the National Park Service. Learn more about how NPS-managed lands and programs provide economic benefits at www.nps.gov.

A new study reveals the significant **economic impact of Maryland museums**, including millions in visitor spending, thousands of jobs, and support for local businesses.
Museums contribute more than history, art, and culture. They also strengthen local economies, support tourism, and create jobs.
A new statewide study commissioned by the **Maryland Museums Association (MMA)** puts numbers behind these contributions. According to the _Economic Impact Study of Maryland Museums_, museums and cultural institutions generated **$705.3 million in economic impact during Fiscal Year 2025**.
The study was released on October 21, 2026, and prepared by Parker Strategy Group.

## Maryland Museums: Key Economic Impact Findings
The study examined the economic contributions of 95 participating museums across Maryland. Researchers measured museum operating and capital spending, as well as visitor spending at local businesses.
Here are some of the key findings:
*   **$705.3 million** in total statewide economic impact.  
*   **4,508 jobs** supported or sustained through museum operations and visitor spending.  
*   **$6.29 returned** to Maryland’s economy for every $1 museums spend directly on operations and capital projects.  
*   **$53.9 million** in estimated state and local tax revenue.  
*   **$504.6 million** in economic output from museum visitor spending.
The total economic impact includes $200.7 million from museum operations and capital spending. Visitor spending accounted for another $504.6 million.
This visitor spending includes dining, lodging, transportation, and retail purchases. These activities also benefit businesses throughout the state.

## Museums Strengthen Maryland’s Communities
The economic impact of Maryland museums extends beyond dollars and jobs.
The report highlights museums as important anchors for tourism economies. It also recognizes their role in workforce development and community infrastructure.
Museums bring visitors to local communities. Those visitors support restaurants, hotels, shops, and other businesses.
In addition, museums create opportunities for learning, cultural engagement, and community connection.
These findings demonstrate why museums are valuable community assets and important contributors to Maryland’s economy.

Museums contribute more than history, art, and culture. They also strengthen local economies, support tourism, and create jobs.
A new statewide study commissioned by the **Maryland Museums Association (MMA)** puts numbers behind these contributions. According to the _Economic Impact Study of Maryland Museums_, museums and cultural institutions generated **$705.3 million in economic impact during Fiscal Year 2025**.
The study was released on October 21, 2026, and prepared by Parker Strategy Group.
texts.1:
## Maryland Museums: Key Economic Impact Findings
The study examined the economic contributions of 95 participating museums across Maryland. Researchers measured museum operating and capital spending, as well as visitor spending at local businesses.
Here are some of the key findings:
*   **$705.3 million** in total statewide economic impact.  
*   **4,508 jobs** supported or sustained through museum operations and visitor spending.  
*   **$6.29 returned** to Maryland’s economy for every $1 museums spend directly on operations and capital projects.  
*   **$53.9 million** in estimated state and local tax revenue.  
*   **$504.6 million** in economic output from museum visitor spending.
The total economic impact includes $200.7 million from museum operations and capital spending. Visitor spending accounted for another $504.6 million.
This visitor spending includes dining, lodging, transportation, and retail purchases. These activities also benefit businesses throughout the state.
texts.2:
## Museums Strengthen Maryland’s Communities
The economic impact of Maryland museums extends beyond dollars and jobs.
The report highlights museums as important anchors for tourism economies. It also recognizes their role in workforce development and community infrastructure.
Museums bring visitors to local communities. Those visitors support restaurants, hotels, shops, and other businesses.
In addition, museums create opportunities for learning, cultural engagement, and community connection.
These findings demonstrate why museums are valuable community assets and important contributors to Maryland’s economy.
